audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.note: Hosted Computers API/SDK/CLI exposes create, list, get, terminals, browser/display, publish/unpublish port, exec, exec_stream, command history, stop, start, delete; no snapshot or fork call. Homepage claims "Pause, resume, and snapshots preserve state" and "Forking: Branch a running sandbox into parallel copies" — these match the open-source local SmolVM runtime (docs.celesto.ai/smolvm/features/snapshots: "A full snapshot captures the VM's CPU state, memory, and disk"), not documented for the hosted cloud. OpenAI Agents integration can persist_workspace() as a tarball (files only, client-side).

harness_api.quote: The harness runs outside the sandbox and continuously learns from every run
harness_api.note: Managed Agents API (ManagedAgentsClient: agents, runs.create/runs.stream SSE, sessions, per-end-user budgets) drives Celesto's own hosted agent harness, which runs outside the sandbox, so it does not drive a harness inside a Computer. `celesto claude|codex|opencode|openclaw|hermes|pi start` are SmolVM CLI launchers that create a (local) sandbox with the agent preinstalled and attach a terminal (agent_harnesses, not an API).

egress_allowlist.quote: Network Control currently supports these two settings. Domain and IP allowlists are not available.
egress_allowlist.note: Only a no-internet mode: network_policy {mode: open|off} (`--no-internet`), fixed at create time and kept across stop/start/restore. No domain or IP lists (level: none/off-only). Off cannot be combined with persistent_home. Local SmolVM has internet_settings allowlists, not the hosted product.

egress_http_rules.quote: Network Control currently supports these two settings. Domain and IP allowlists are not available.

ingress_rules.quote: Services inside a Celesto computer are private by default.
ingress_rules.note: You choose which ports (1024-65535, max four at a time) get a public HTTPS URL and can unpublish them. Published URLs have no auth or IP allowlist: "Treat published URLs as public. If the service exposes sensitive data or actions, add authentication to the service before sharing the URL."

guest_firewall.note: Hardware-isolated Firecracker microVMs with own kernel ("Hardware-isolated microVMs"); root inside not explicitly documented for hosted computers (user is `ohm`).

secret_proxy.quote: Computer(cpus, memory, disk, template_id, template_version, persistent_home, network_policy)
secret_proxy.note: Hosted Computer.create() only accepts sizing, template, persistent_home, and network_policy params -- no secrets/credential-proxy parameter or endpoint. The docs' only secret/credential-injection mechanism (env_vars=, vm.set_env_vars/unset_env_vars/list_env_vars, injected via SSH into /etc/profile.d/smolvm_env.sh or Windows HKCU\Environment) belongs to the local/self-hosted SmolVM product, not the hosted Computers API, and even there it is plain env-var injection, not an HTTP-request-signing secret proxy. No first-party proxy that injects credentials into outbound HTTP calls without exposing them to the sandbox is documented anywhere for Celesto; matches definition of secret_proxy=false (secrets only as env vars/mounted files).

image_oci.quote: Sandbox template ID. Pass `coding-agent` when your agent needs common coding tools already installed.
image_oci.note: Hosted Computers API only creates from Celesto's own fixed templates (`scratch`, `coding-agent`); no parameter accepts a user-supplied Docker/OCI image. Dockerfile-based custom images (`DockerRootfsBuilder`, `Celesto.from_image`) are a local SmolVM feature, not documented for the hosted cloud product.

nested_virt.note: derived: every /dev/kvm reference in the docs is about the host needing KVM to boot the Firecracker/QEMU microVM itself; nothing documents /dev/kvm being exposed inside the guest for nested virtualization.

desktop.quote: Use `Celesto.desktop()` when your agent needs the whole desktop environment, such as a window manager, visible apps, or a VNC-compatible computer-use driver.
desktop.note: not offered on the hosted Cloud Computers product: the hosted `Computer` response only exposes `connection.ssh` and `connection.access_url` (docs.celesto.ai/cloud/computers). `Celesto.desktop()`/`viewer_url`/`display_url` (VNC desktop) is documented only for local SmolVM sandboxes.

computer_use.quote: VNC URL for desktop viewers and computer-use agents that need direct screen control.
computer_use.note: not offered on the hosted Cloud Computers product for the same reason as desktop: the VNC `display_url` computer-use driver endpoint is documented for local SmolVM `Celesto.browser()/desktop()` sandboxes, not the hosted Computers API.

anti_bot.quote: The Computers API gives your code or agent an isolated Linux computer. You create a computer, run work inside it, and then stop, start, or delete it when your workflow is done.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Celesto is a generic sandboxed-computer/coding-agent runtime; no stealth/fingerprint-evasion feature is documented anywhere.

captcha_solving.quote: The Computers API gives your code or agent an isolated Linux computer. You create a computer, run work inside it, and then stop, start, or delete it when your workflow is done.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature or API is documented on any Celesto page.

egress_ip_type.quote: `open` Connect to the internet. This is the default.
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound traffic just goes through the normal cloud host's network path (open/off toggle only); no static, residential, or mobile IP option is documented, so it is ordinary shared datacenter egress.

snapshot.quote: Celesto keeps both the computer root disk and workspace state across stop and start.
snapshot.note: Stop/start preserves files/disk (root disk + CelestoFS workspace), not a running-process memory image — stopping actually shuts the VM down. No documented snapshot/fork call exists in the hosted SDK (see snapshot_on_demand evidence in the card), so this is filesystem-level persistence, not a memory snapshot.

snapshot_auto.quote: The simplest way to keep state is to stop a computer instead of deleting it. A stopped computer keeps its workspace, which means the files and folders inside the computer.
snapshot_auto.note: No extra API call is needed to save state: calling `stop()` automatically preserves the root disk and workspace, and `start()` automatically restores it.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: The hosted Computers SDK/CLI exposes create/list/get/stop/start/delete/run/publish-port/terminal only — there is no fork or snapshot call, so cloned machines with restored in-memory process state are not available (matches the card's existing snapshot_on_demand evidence).

wake_on_request.quote: The CLI can start a stopped computer automatically when you run a command or open a terminal.
wake_on_request.note: Auto-start only happens when your own CLI/SDK call (`run`, `ssh`) explicitly triggers it — there is no evidence a stopped computer wakes itself when an inbound HTTP/network request arrives at a previously published port.

volume_attach.quote: Celesto sandboxes include a large durable filesystem for workspace data.
volume_attach.note: Storage is limited to the resizable root disk (`disk_size_mb`, set at create time) plus the automatically-included CelestoFS workspace mount; there is no API to attach a separate, independently manageable extra volume.

volume_shared.quote: CelestoFS is mounted inside the sandbox so programs can use normal file operations from the guest.
volume_shared.note: CelestoFS workspace storage is documented as one computer's own durable filesystem; nothing describes mounting the same volume on multiple running computers simultaneously.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Stop it to pause work and keep the files inside it. Start it when you want to continue.
auto_stop_idle.note: Lifecycle docs describe only explicit `stop()`/`start()` calls; no idle-timeout auto-stop/auto-sleep behavior is documented for hosted computers.

live_resize.quote: CPU and memory must match one of these named sizes ... Omit both CPU and memory to use the template default.
live_resize.note: CPU/memory/disk are chosen once at `Computer()` creation time; no documented API resizes a running computer's vCPU/RAM without recreating it.

agent_harnesses.quote: Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, and Pi inside a Celesto sandbox with full permissions
agent_harnesses.note: Preinstalled coding-agent presets (`celesto claude|codex|opencode|openclaw|hermes|pi start`) are local SmolVM CLI launchers requiring local virtualization. The hosted Cloud Computers template list is only `scratch` and `coding-agent` (which installs generic dev tools — git/node/npm — not a preinstalled coding-agent harness).

own_agent_api.quote: Managed agents let you run AI agents for your end users, with per-user budgets and an audit trail. You define an agent once, then call it on behalf of one of your users each time they interact with your product.
own_agent_api.note: The Managed Agents API drives an agent that YOU define (via the Agentor framework), not a first-party Celesto-built browser/computer-use/research agent.

mcp_server.quote: CelestoMCPHub is a context manager that provides access to Celesto AI's MCP Hub, which aggregates multiple MCP servers and their tools into a single endpoint.
mcp_server.note: CelestoMCPHub/LiteMCP let you build or aggregate MCP servers as agent *tools*; no MCP server ships that itself exposes control of Celesto Computers/sandboxes (create/run/stop/etc.) to an MCP client.

lang_python.note: Python 3 runs out of the box in Celesto computers, and the first-party SDK itself is Python (`pip install celesto`).

lang_node.quote: Create a `coding-agent` computer. This template comes with Node, npm, and git already installed, which is what most web apps need.
lang_node.note: Node.js/npm ship in the `coding-agent` template, and a first-party TypeScript/Node SDK (`@celestoai/sdk`) exists.

public_ipv4.quote: Publishing a port gives your computer a public HTTPS URL.
public_ipv4.note: Reachability is via a per-port HTTPS URL through Celesto's proxy, not a dedicated public IPv4 address per machine; no public IPv4 allocation is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Network Control currently supports these two settings. Domain and IP allowlists are not available.
static_egress_ip.note: Only an open/off outbound toggle is documented; no fixed/static outbound IP feature exists.

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only shared-vCPU/RAM/disk sizes are sold; no GPU size, GPU pricing, or GPU mention appears anywhere on the site or docs.

windows.quote: The Computers API gives your code or agent an isolated Linux computer.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The hosted product is explicitly a Linux sandbox (demo output shows `Linux celesto 6.8.0 x86_64 GNU/Linux`); no Windows guest option exists.

macos.quote: The Computers API gives your code or agent an isolated Linux computer.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No macOS guest option is documented anywhere.

arm64.note: The hosted Cloud demo/output is x86_64. arm64 boot images are only mentioned for local SmolVM builds (e.g. `codex-v0.0.31-arm64-qemu`); no arm64 option is documented for hosted Cloud computers.

byoc.quote: Open-source core. Self-host or use our cloud.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Celesto offers exactly two deployment modes — fully self-hosted open-source SmolVM on your own infra, or Celesto's own managed multi-tenant cloud — not a managed deployment into the customer's own cloud account.

sso.quote: The command prompts for your API key and stores it in your operating system's secure credential store: Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, or Secret Service on Linux.
sso.note: Authentication is API-key based only; no SAML/OIDC SSO is documented.

soc2.quote: Celesto AI is currently operating in Research Mode. Features may be experimental and subject to change. Do not use the services for regulated or high-risk workloads unless we have an appropriate agreement in place.
soc2.note: No SOC 2 report, badge, or trust/compliance page is published anywhere on celesto.ai or docs.celesto.ai. The Terms explicitly flag the product as 'Research Mode' and tell customers not to use it for regulated workloads without a separate agreement, consistent with no SOC 2 attestation existing yet.

hipaa.quote: Celesto AI is currently operating in Research Mode... Do not use the services for regulated or high-risk workloads unless we have an appropriate agreement in place.
hipaa.note: No HIPAA-eligibility or BAA-availability statement appears anywhere on the site, docs, privacy policy, or subprocessor registry. The Terms' explicit warning against regulated/high-risk workloads without a separate agreement is consistent with no BAA being offered.

eu_data_residency.quote: Amazon Web Services, Inc. | Cloud infrastructure (compute, storage, networking) | United States and other regions. Google LLC | Cloud infrastructure, managed services, and Google Analytics 4 | United States.
eu_data_residency.note: No region selector or EU region is documented anywhere for Cloud Computers (the card's own `regions: []`), and the subprocessor registry lists infrastructure providers as US-based ('United States' / 'United States and other regions'), not EU. The Privacy Policy's 'International Transfers' clause (Standard Contractual Clauses for cross-border transfers) further implies data leaves the EU/UK by default rather than staying resident in an EU region.

max_session_h.quote: Stop it to pause work and keep the files inside it. Start it when you want to continue.
max_session_h.note: No documented maximum session/run duration, forced eviction, or wall-clock cap exists for a running Computer; lifecycle is entirely explicit stop()/start()/delete() (auto_stop_idle is also false). Treated as no limit -- a computer runs until the caller stops it or capacity/billing issues intervene. The 30-day retention note in the card applies only to a STOPPED computer's root disk, not to how long a RUNNING session may last.

cpu_class.quote: Micro $0.03/hour 1 shared vCPU · 2 GB RAM · 20 GB root disk ... Large $0.16/hour 4 shared vCPU · 16 GB RAM · 60 GB root disk ... XL $0.32/hour 8 shared vCPU · 32 GB RAM · 100 GB root disk
cpu_class.note: Every size in the only pricing mode ('on-demand') is explicitly labeled 'shared vCPU' on the pricing page; no dedicated/reserved-core tier is offered.
